title: Narratives about vaccination in the age of fake news: A content analysis on social networks
screen_reason: Content analysis (in Portuguese) of the 100 most-engaged links containing the word 'vacina' on social networks between 22 May 2018 and 21 May 2019 (final analysed corpus 87 links, retrieved via BuzzSumo across Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest and Reddit). One of the coded dimensions, 'caráter da informação' (character of the information), classifies each link as true/verifiable, fact-checking, distorted or false, so the paper reports the share of items judged FALSE (5 links, 5.7%) and DISTORTED (3 links, 3.4%) with an explicit denominator. That is an external veracity judgement against recognised sources, hence CONTENT rather than QUALITY.

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Authors' own coding using an adapted version of the content-analysis protocol of the Ibero-American Network for Monitoring and Training in Science Journalism (Massarani; Ramalho, 2012). True information is defined as "verificáveis com base em fontes reconhecidas nas áreas em questão, seja científica, social ou política" [verifiable on the basis of recognised sources in the relevant field, whether scientific, social or political]. The protocol was applied by one author (Modesto) and analysed by the team; no inter-coder reliability statistic, double coding or blinding is reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Selecionamos um corpus formado pelas 100 publicações com a palavra-chave “vacina”, com o maior número de compartilhamentos, curtidas e comentários em redes sociais ao longo de um ano. A coleta foi feita por meio do BuzzSumo, ferramenta que avalia a performance de conteúdos nas plataformas Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest e Reddit. Os resultados foram filtrados pelos seguintes critérios: (1) data de publicação entre 22 de maio de 2018 e 21 de maio de 2019 (12 meses); (2) apenas publicações em língua portuguesa; e (3) somente publicações contendo links, visando permitir sua análise. [We selected a corpus of the 100 publications with the keyword 'vaccine' with the highest number of shares, likes and comments on social networks over one year, collected via BuzzSumo, a tool that assesses content performance on Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest and Reddit, filtered by: (1) publication date between 22 May 2018 and 21 May 2019; (2) Portuguese-language publications only; (3) only publications containing links.]
estimates.notes: The unit is the link/item, not the share, so this is CONTENT even though the corpus was selected by engagement; the rank-truncated top-100 selection is captured by denom_selection = curated. country_norm = Brazil: the sampling filter was Portuguese LANGUAGE, but the study is explicitly about the Brazilian debate ('avaliar as informações acerca das vacinas que circulam nas redes sociais no Brasil'). Final corpus 87 of the 100 links after 13 unrecoverable pages. 5/87 = 5.7%, matching the paper's own percentage. The PDF renders these pages in two interleaved columns, so only a single physical line can be quoted as one contiguous span. The quoted fragment comes from the Considerações finais sentence "não se pode desconsiderar a ocorrência de conteúdos falsos (5,7%) e distorcidos (3,4%)" [one cannot disregard the occurrence of false (5.7%) and distorted (3.4%) content]; the fuller statement in the Results is: Contudo, é preciso ressaltar que cinco (5,7%) dos links mais compartilhados foram identificados como falsos, e três (3,4%) como distorcidos. [However, it must be stressed that five (5.7%) of the most-shared links were identified as false, and three (3.4%) as distorted.]

estimates.notes: definition_variant = true: same country x platform x measure cell as the 'false' row, but a looser veracity category (distorted rather than outright false). The two categories are mutually exclusive in the paper's coding, so they must not be pooled by addition here; a combined 8/87 = 9.2% would be a cross-category sum, which R8 forbids. Quoted fragment is the second half of the Results sentence: Contudo, é preciso ressaltar que cinco (5,7%) dos links mais compartilhados foram identificados como falsos, e três (3,4%) como distorcidos. [However, it must be stressed that five (5.7%) of the most-shared links were identified as false, and three (3.4%) as distorted.] Two-column rendering prevents quoting the whole sentence as one contiguous span.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The complementary categories of the same coding are not misinformation shares and would require complements/sums I computed: 81.6% true/verifiable, 6.9% fact-checking, 2.3% (two) fictional contents. Only the false and distorted shares are extracted. (2) Stance coding is not veracity: 'posicionamentos pró-vacina (87,4%), neutros (6,9%), com argumentos contra e a favor (3,4%) e contrários à vacinação (2,3%)' [pro-vaccine 87.4%, neutral 6.9%, mixed 3.4%, anti-vaccination 2.3%]. An anti-vaccination stance is not by itself a false-content classification, so no row. (3) Framing, treatment and actor percentages (e.g. 'politicas publicas' 44.8%, scientific-term explanation 24.1%, controversies 23%, no author identification 41.4%) are content characteristics, not veracity. (4) Figures the paper cites from elsewhere, excluded by R8: the Avaaz/SBIm survey (67% of respondents identified at least one factually inaccurate statement as true; 57% of the 13% who did not vaccinate justified it with beliefs deemed incorrect; 73% of those who believed false information use social networks and messaging apps) and the Wellcome Global Monitor 2018 percentages. Those are also belief measures, excluded on that ground too. (5) The paper reports that all five false links carried no author identification, but gives no further prevalence denominators.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Corpus: the 100 Portuguese-language links containing the keyword 'vacina' with the most shares, likes and comments on social networks between 22 May 2018 and 21 May 2019, identified with the free trial version of BuzzSumo (which aggregates Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest and Reddit engagement) on 21 May 2019; deactivated pages partially recovered via the Wayback Machine, leaving a final analysed sample of 87 links. Coding used an adapted version of the Ibero-American Network for Monitoring and Training in Science Journalism protocol (Massarani; Ramalho, 2012) across five sections (general characteristics, theme, narrative, treatment, actors), applied by one author (Modesto) and analysed by the team. No inter-coder reliability statistics, no double coding and no blinding are reported; engagement ranking depends on undisclosed platform algorithms, which the authors acknowledge.
rob.item6_quote: No âmbito da pesquisa, compreendemos informações distorcidas como aquelas que trazem informações corretas, mas fora de contexto ou com manchetes que induzem a uma interpretação equivocada. Já informações falsas seriam os conteúdos enganosos, tais como as fake news “Adolescente virgem diz que ficou grávida após tomar vacina contra gripe” ou “Trump alerta: a vacina da gripe é a maior fraude na história da medicina”. [In this research we understand distorted information as that which carries correct information but out of context, or with headlines that induce a mistaken interpretation. False information would be deceptive content, such as the fake news 'Virgin teenager says she got pregnant after taking the flu vaccine' or 'Trump warns: the flu vaccine is the biggest fraud in the history of medicine'.]
